name: Leonid Brezhnev
summary: Brezhnev defended developed socialism, public ownership, social guarantees and the Communist Party’s leading role. He pursued arms-control agreements and peaceful coexistence while asserting a right to intervene against threats to socialism and suppressing domestic dissent.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He names general and complete disarmament as an ultimate goal, but in the same speeches commits to a strong army and military service, so words and record pull apart.

arms-reduction.rationale: He advocated negotiations to reduce military danger and avert war.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: He says capitalism adapts to new conditions and keeps developing, but that this is not stabilisation and its general crisis keeps deepening; the evidence points both ways.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He linked imperialism and militarism with capitalist social relations.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He described socialism as succeeding the productive achievements of capitalism.

central-planning.rationale: He retained the planned economy as the framework for socialist development.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He treats rule of some nations over others as oppression and enslavement, and backs armed struggles against the colonialists.

class-collaboration.rationale: He backs the class struggle of the working class against monopoly capital in capitalist countries, including strike waves, and condemns opportunism.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: He says exploiter classes are gone and the Soviet state is a state of the whole people with the working class leading, with no class basis for restoration.

collective-defense.rationale: He describes the Warsaw Treaty and bilateral treaties as a system of mutual allied commitments of a new type and the socialist community as a military alliance.

collective-farming.rationale: He praised large-scale mechanised agriculture built on collectivist principles.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He condemns colonial exploitation as a policy of imperialism and says Soviet policy is opposed to the oppression and enslavement of peoples.

conscription.rationale: He praises military service in the Soviet Army as a school of combat skill, ideological and physical steeling and discipline.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: He sought better pensions, medical care and benefits.

defeat-communism.rationale: He described communist construction as the continuing objective of Soviet policy.

defend-planned-state.rationale: He defended intervention to preserve socialist gains against restoration.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He endorsed its revolutionary historical role but said the USSR had become a state of the whole people.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He calls the Warsaw Treaty Organisation the main centre for coordinating the foreign policy of the socialist states and speaks of the bloc's military alliance as a pillar.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He explicitly rejected equal wages and pensions regardless of skill or work.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He asks the Congress to make West Siberian gas and oil production and transport to the west the most important elements of the energy programme, and earlier boasts of oil output growth.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He reports that the nuclear power industry is expanding fast and asks to expand it more rapidly, including fast-neutron reactors and a start on fusion.

farm-price-support.rationale: He reports and defends stable multi-year state procurement plans and higher purchase prices for farm produce after the March plenum, with the Politburo keeping them largely in place.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: He defended distribution according to work rather than unearned private ownership.

independent-unions.rationale: He describes Soviet unions as acting with the Party's guidance as a school of administration and communism, and the Party's role over them as leading, though without petty tutelage.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: He asserted a common socialist duty to stop capitalist restoration in allied states.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He demands Israeli withdrawal from occupied Arab lands and condemns Zionism, but his 1981 report says the security and sovereignty of all states in the region including Israel should be guaranteed.

job-guarantee.rationale: He upheld the constitutionally guaranteed right to employment.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He promoted planned socialist production over capitalist allocation.

military-superiority.rationale: His 26th Congress report says the USSR has not sought and does not seek military superiority, but will not permit the other side to gain it; he states a policy of parity.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: He rejected proposals to eliminate autonomous and union republics.

moral-incentives.rationale: He keeps payment by work as a major material incentive and criticises the egalitarian approach, while saying moral incentives should be raised alongside, not as a replacement.

national-self-determination.rationale: He subordinated national sovereignty to the interests of the world socialist movement.

one-party-rule.rationale: He defended the Communist Party’s leading role in socialist society.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He argues that socialist democracy means drawing millions into running state bodies, production and unions, and backs electors' mandates and work collectives.

party-controls-media.rationale: His government confiscated independent literature and punished unauthorised political expression.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He calls democratic centralism an immutable law of Party life and says Party discipline must be strengthened.

party-own-road.rationale: He conditioned national parties’ freedom on the common interests of the socialist bloc.

patriotic-education.rationale: He calls military-patriotic education of the young one of the major tasks in moulding the rising generation and says the Party sees it as a sacred duty.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: He joins loyalty to the Motherland with communist convictions and internationalism, and calls the army's men patriots and internationalists.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: He defended personal holdings alongside socialist productive property.

positive-liberty.rationale: He argued social rights make freedom substantive rather than merely formal.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He describes capitalist rule as intensified exploitation of working people by monopolies and says exploitation of man by man ended in the USSR with the end of private ownership of the means of production.

public-ownership.rationale: He defended public ownership throughout the economy as socialism’s foundation.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: His 24th Congress report presents the raising of the minimum wage to 60 roubles as an achievement of the plan period he led, and the 1968 speech lists raising it among the measures taken.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He endorses the former colonies' call for a new international economic order, restructuring on a democratic basis of equality, while warning against reducing it to a rich North versus poor South.

right-to-secede.rationale: He explicitly retained republics’ formal secession right despite coercive limits on sovereignty.

second-chamber.rationale: He rejected abolishing the Soviet of Nationalities.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: He identified social ownership and people’s political power as the substance of socialism.

socialism-one-country.rationale: He says developed socialism has been built in the USSR with a stable and indestructible social system, contradicting the view that it cannot last in one country alone.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He prioritised modern industries and productivity through the party’s economic strategy.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He puts the USSR at the head of the Warsaw Treaty bloc as an alliance of socialist states against imperialist military blocs.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His leadership imprisoned, exiled and forcibly hospitalised dissidents.

unions-good.rationale: In his speech to the 15th Trade Union Congress he says unions defend working people and take direct part in raising production and in economic management; in the capitalist world he backs union struggle.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He defended free medical care as a socialist guarantee.

vanguard-party.rationale: He attributed socialist progress to the party’s ideological and political leadership.

worker-ownership.rationale: He endorsed collective and state property with an expanded role for work collectives.

workers-nation.rationale: He calls proletarian internationalism one of the main principles of Marxism-Leninism and warns against interpreting it so that little is left of it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: He supported wider work-collective participation in enterprise decisions.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: He states that imperialists plunder peoples of Asia, Africa and Latin America and extract thousands of millions of dollars from the Third World, and that pillaging resources and exploiting labour remain an inalienable feature of imperialism.

notes:
Downloaded constitutional speech searched across themes. The scanned 1981 report had no extractable text and was not used to assign unsupported energy or technology positions. Constitutional claims and coercive practice are distinguished; all nulls reviewed and no historical extrapolations added. Auditor identification: the runtime identifies this assistant as GPT-6/Codex but does not expose an exact version or variant; gpt-6 is the available identifier, not an asserted variant. Final wording review left freedom-as-non-domination unknown because the available record addresses a related, narrower or different proposition.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 30 answers taken from it, 25 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass (Sonnet) from his own speeches in English translation: Following Lenin's Course (1972 and 1972-75 volumes), Congress reports (24th, 25th, 26th), the 1967 jubilee report and the 1977 constitution report. Texts are in scratchpad/sources/leonid-brezhnev/. Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, ecology, technology, means. Ecology, technology, and culture are thin: the speeches say little that settles the statements (the 26th Congress scan is garbled in the OCR pages on environment and the Food Programme). Not found as his own words: his stand on religion and the state, media control, elections beyond the party list, and term limits, so those stay null. Words versus record: he claims the republics' right to secede and general disarmament as goals while the record shows neither exercised, so those are 0 at low. Intervention answers rest on his 1968 Warsaw speech and 24th Congress report, where he justifies the Czechoslovak action himself; the Afghanistan invasion is left out because no text of his in these sources explains it.
